topic: Fair testing, variables, and measurement reliability
key_concepts: A fair test compares a control group and an experimental group.
The experimental group differs from the control group by only one variable.
The independent variable is the factor that is changed.
The dependent variable is the factor that is measured.
Control variables are all other factors kept the same.
A control group provides a standard for comparison.
A hypothesis is an educated guess tested by experiment.
Doing at least three trials or replication makes a fair test more reliable.
Accuracy means closeness to the true value.
Precision means closeness of repeated measurements to each other.
Accurate observing, measuring, and recording are part of scientific investigations.
Pollution can harm river water and community health.
